newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says leave new bank licences to new govt.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says leave new bank licences to new govt.

text.p: Outgoing Thai Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa reiterated on Thursday that he will not approve any new banking licences during his remaining tenure to avoid being accused of corruption.
Banharn told Reuters in an interview he will leave the matter to the new government which will come on board after the November 17 general election.
"I will not touch this issue while I'm in office. If I approved the licences, I will be accused of corruption," he said.
Thailand plans to award the first new banking licences in about two decades as part of an effort to liberalise the financial sector.

The issue caused a scandal several months ago after former Justice Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung alleged that politicians were receiving kickbacks worth about 750 million baht (US$30 million) for each new licence.
Former finance minister Bodi Chunnananda's resignation earlier this month was shrouded with talk that he stepped down due to conflict on the timing of bank licences approval.
But Banharn denied the allegations, saying Bodi left for personal reasons.

"He (Bodi) intended to resign since the parliament was dissolved on September 27," said Banharn who dissolved the lower house a week after he was forced by his coalition partners to resign from the premiership.
Banharn said he asked Bodi to stay on for a few weeks to find his replacement.
"That why I approached deputy central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawasdi to take a deputy finance portfolio. The rumour on banking licence is not true," he said.
Chaiyawat was named finance minister after Bodi announced his resignation on October 14. ($1.00=25 baht)
